**Verified rule from demo and solved test:** Identify enclosed background-color cells inside a same-color outline/figure, and recolor those interior cells to 4. Keep outline pixels, other colors, and the grid dimensions unchanged. Do not fill open regions or extend markings.

**Demo evidence:** Demo input was 17x28 with background 9 and patterns drawn in 2. For example, a 2-pixel-wide rectangular cavity enclosed inside a 2 outline was filled with 4. Only enclosed interior cells changed; the 2-colored frame and all other objects/pixels remained intact. In the output, rows 2–4, columns 14–15 (zero-based) are 4; likewise enclosed interiors rows 3–4, cols 1–2 and cols 8–9 were filled. Open shapes/lines were unchanged.

**Solved test evidence:** 26x12 grid, background 1 with a 9 pattern. The compact top motif has two enclosed 1-colored holes at zero-based (row 3,col 7) and (row 4,col 7), both changed to 4. All 9s and the long vertical 9 stem below remain unchanged. Submission explicitly scored CORRECT.

**Reusable procedure:** For each closed loop/outline, locate enclosed cells of its background and change those to 4. Preserve boundaries and open/background areas. In this family color numbers/background may vary; demo provides the target fill color (here 4).
